changes.title: AWS CloudFormation Service-Managed StackSets adds custom execution roles with nested stacks support
changes.detail: AWS CloudFormation StackSets now supports custom execution roles for service-managed stack sets, which enables you to scope the permissions StackSets uses in each target AWS account. StackSets deploys the same infrastructure, such as networking and security settings, across thousands of accounts and Regions in one operation. With a custom execution role, you can also use nested stacks, macros, and transforms in service-managed stack sets, which allows you to deploy the reusable templates you use for individual stacks across your organization. changes.title: Amazon Aurora MySQL 8.4.12 is now generally available
changes.detail: Starting today, Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition 8.4 supports MySQL 8.4.12. This release includes several security enhancements and bug fixes. We recommend upgrading to the newer minor versions to accept fixes for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in prior versions of MySQL and to benefit from bug fixes, performance improvements, and new functionality added by community MySQL. For more details, refer to the Aurora MySQL 8.4 and MySQL 8.4.12 release notes. You can upgrade your databases during scheduled maintenance windows using automatic minor version upgrades. changes.title: Introducing Amazon EC2 T9g instances based on Graviton5
changes.detail: AWS is announcing the general availability of new low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T9g instances, which offer the best price performance among general-purpose EC2 instances. These instances are powered by AWS Graviton5 processors and built on the latest sixth generation AWS Nitro cards. T9g instances deliver up to 45% better price performance compared to previous generation T4g instances, and offer four sizes: nano, micro, small, and medium.
